p: "He made the letter Kuf king over laughter, etc.,
and Adar in the year, and the spleen in the soul."
and this He made king over laughter;
and therefore he ascribed to it

But according to this, he should have said

and therefore he said to him,
for in this world it is forbidden

And it is known that every letter,
in the place where it is first mentioned in the Torah,
the root of that letter's holiness,
as is evident in the Gemara
That is, the letter Kuf is "kadosh,"
as they said in the Gemara
and supernal wisdom is supernal holiness;
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג קעו, ב)
That is, Chochmah is the Written Torah,
is the utterance "Let there be light,"
and "light" is written in it five times,
corresponding to the five Chumashim of the Torah,

which the Ramban wrote in his novellae

that is, a spirit from that holiness above.

which is what the letter Kuf indicates,
in the word "vayikra": "He called the light day."
That is, the tip of the Yud
as they said in the holy Zohar
and it includes the upper and lower holiness,
the Written Torah and Torah she'b'al peh,
and then is the time for the revelation of joy.

which is propitious for the eradication of Amalek,

and when he is wiped out,
And this is why it was formed with Kuf and with laughter,

For the essence of the serpent's enticement
was in eating for bodily pleasure,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה גָּרַם וְהֵבִיא הָעֶצֶב

and about this "ledorosam" is written defective,

a dwelling for them on Shabbos

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Sod Yesharim, Parshas Shekalim 4 — “When all the clarifications are complete … through this laughter they will see the connection of all Yisrael's service, which in this world looks like laughter and small things.” The Radziner Rebbe, citing his father, explains why the revelation of joy waits for the future. Only then will it be seen that even the humblest service of Yisrael is rooted in Atika.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Maharal, Netzach Yisrael 23 — “Tefillin are a crown and splendor upon a person… I rejoice in the Cause Himself, that He is my Master and His Name is called upon me… the true bond is the tefillin.” Maharal gives the reason Abaye's answer worked. One who is bound to his Source may rejoice openly, because his joy comes from that bond and not from himself. This is Rav Tzadok's “bound to the root.”

paragraphs.text: Shemot Rabbah 23:1 — “Although You have existed forever, Your throne was not established and You were not known in Your world until Your children sang.... A king fought a war and won, and they made him Augustus. They said: ‘Before the war you were a king; now we have made you Augustus.’ What difference in honor is there? The king stands upon the platform, while Augustus sits. Thus Israel said: ‘Before You created Your world You existed; since You created it You exist, but, as it were, standing.... When You stood at the sea and we sang before You with az, Your sovereignty became settled and Your throne established.’”

paragraphs.text: Commentary attributed to Raavad on Sefer Yetzirah 5:1 — “Laughter is assigned to Naphtali, as it is said, ‘Of Naphtali he said: Naphtali, satisfied with favor and full...’; thought is assigned to Issachar.... Sleep is assigned to Benjamin, as it is said, ‘He dwells between his shoulders.’... By all these twelve qualities we describe the activity of the blessed God: seeing—‘The Lord saw’; hearing—‘The Lord heard’; smelling—‘The Lord smelled’; speech—‘The Lord spoke’.... Laughter—‘He who sits in heaven laughs’; thought—‘The Lord planned to destroy’; sleep—‘Awake! Why do You sleep, Lord?’”

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Chanukah 18 — “The letter ayin first mentioned in the Torah comes after the word ‘and darkness was upon…’ … there is the root of the letter's power, as they learned (Bava Kamma 55a) regarding tes.” Rav Tzadok applies the same rule to the ayin of Teves. The first place a letter appears marks its root, whether that root is the light of the kuf or the darkness that Teves's anger must repair.

paragraphs.text: Zohar III, 169b (Shelach) — “‘On the third day Esther clothed herself in royalty’—she clothed herself in that likeness of the other world. Royalty is the holy spirit, for the kingdom of heaven sends forth a spirit from the air of that world, and Esther clothed herself in it. When she entered before King Achashverosh and he saw that garment of light, her appearance seemed like an angel of God, and his soul departed from him for a moment. Mordechai was likewise, as it is written, ‘Mordechai went out from before the king in royal clothing’: royal clothing indeed, the likeness of that world. Therefore it is written, ‘The fear of Mordechai fell upon them’—the fear of Mordechai, and not the fear of Achashverosh.”

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Kav HaYashar 93 — “When the Beis HaMikdash stood, two lights shone for Yisrael from two upper worlds, of which it says ‘Let there be light, and there was light’… and twice ‘or’ equals in gematria sechok.” The gematria links laughter (414) to the light of the first day in so many words. It supports Rav Tzadok's reading that the kuf's rule over laughter means the revealing of the hidden first light.

paragraphs.text: Machberet HaKodesh, Shaar HaShabbos, Likkutim, 34a, column 2 — “Know that of all a person eats during the week, the greater part goes to the external forces, and it contains no spirituality except in the portion necessary to nourish the soul so that it does not separate. Whoever adds beyond this adds strength to the evil inclination. What he eats on Shabbos, however, is entirely spiritual: even if he eats more than necessary, it is absorbed into his limbs.” The checked passage is in the original collection's Shabbos gate, under Likkutim, in the discussion of eating. Rav Tzadok uses its contrast between ordinary and Shabbos eating to explain how bodily enjoyment can be sanctified and the serpent's damage repaired on Shabbos.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Resisei Layla 55:8 — “Together with blessing there must also be holiness, so that the illumination of the face remains bounded and distinct and does not become frivolous joy.... Among Israel, on the contrary, it produces holiness in the heart. The light of the face that testifies to strength within the heart comes from no frivolous tranquility, but from tranquility filled with holiness.... Sabbath’s blessing is received through prayer.... Holiness is through Kiddush over wine, which gladdens the heart and produces frivolous joy in those who stray through it; but wine of a commandment, on the contrary, produces holiness in the heart and restraint from worldly frivolity.”

paragraphs.text: Connection: The maamar says that even bodily enjoyment on Sabbath can repair the serpent’s corruption of eating. This parallel gives the controlling distinction: the same physical wine can produce frivolity or, when received through the mitzvah of Kiddush, a joy governed by holiness.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Zohar I 48b — “That additional soul… through it they rejoice, and all weekday matters, all pains and distresses, are forgotten from them, as it says, ‘On the day Hashem gives you rest from your sadness and your anger.’” The Zohar names the means by which Shabbos “adds no sorrow.” The neshamah yeseirah, drawn from the World to Come, wipes away the grief that the serpent brought.

paragraphs.text: Mekhilta deRabbi Yishmael, Vayassa, on Exodus 16:28 (current chapter 6; cited as 5) — “Rabbi Yehoshua says: The Holy One, blessed be He, said to Moses: ‘Moses, tell Israel: I brought you out of Egypt, split the sea for you, brought down the manna for you, brought up the well for you, brought you quails, fought Amalek for you, and performed miracles and mighty deeds for you. Until when will you refuse to keep My commandments and My teachings? Perhaps you say that I imposed many commandments upon you? I imposed this Sabbath upon you at Marah to keep it, and you did not keep it! Perhaps you ask what reward one who keeps the Sabbath receives? Scripture says: ‘Happy is the person who does this... who keeps the Sabbath from desecrating it and guards his hand from doing any evil.’ Thus we learn that whoever keeps the Sabbath despite hardship is saved from transgression.’” The Beeri edition reads “keeps the Sabbath despite hardship, is saved from transgression.” The manuscript quotes the related reading “whoever keeps the Sabbath is distanced from transgression.”

paragraphs.text: Pri Etz Chaim, Gate of the Sabbath 1 — “There is no person who does not receive an additional nefesh, ruach and neshamah, according to his allotted share. A person must direct his intention so that some of this addition remains with him for the weekdays. Through this his ways will be set right, if he directs his intention properly; he is assured that he will not sin, that sins will not come about through him, and that the evil inclination will not accuse him. Everything depends upon the intention.”

paragraphs.text: Rashi on Deuteronomy 25:18 — “Another interpretation: it is the language of cold and heat. He cooled you and made you lukewarm after your boiling heat. All the nations feared to fight against you; he came and began, showing the way to others. This is comparable to a boiling bath into which no creature could descend. A reckless person came and jumped into it: although he was scalded, he cooled it for others.”
